newsitem.title: REUNION: New demonstrations on French Indian Ocean island.
newsitem.headline: New demonstrations on French Indian Ocean island.

text.p: New clashes broke out on Monday on the French Indian Ocean island of Reunion where thousands of civil servants and students continued protests against government plans to cut officials' pay.
Eyewitnesses said two people were hurt when police fired tear gas at several thousand protesters who surrounded the island's international airport.
The protesters surrounded the airport for six hours, preventing 1,000 passengers from leaving a stifling terminal hall.
Police evacuated a sick child by helicopter before the siege was lifted.

Dozens of cars were set on fire, shops looted and 28 people arrested in a first outbreak of violence last Thursday when groups of youths went on a rampage in the dilapidated Chaudron neighbourhood of the usually quiet tropical city, police said.

The main reason for the protests is resentment at government plans to start phasing out the extra 53 percent in salaries paid to civil servants stationed in France's overseas possessions, including those locally recruited.
Reunion, with a mixed population of 600,000 Creoles, Indians, Chinese and Europeans is broadly divided into two societies living side by side.
One is made up of people on the government payroll, ranging from top officials to sanitation workers, who have a European standard of living because of salaries higher than those in France
The other lives in poverty because of massive unemployment in the failing sugar cane industry.
